sources.title: Scalar shared-parameter derivative and fixed-depth objective boundary
sources.details: For the word problem, 2+3−1=4. With s0=0 and sr=sr−1+w, substitution yields s1=w, s2=2w, s3=3w. Thus L3=(3w−1)^2 and dL3/dw=2(3w−1)·3. At w=0.2: s3=0.6, L3=(−0.4)^2=0.16, derivative=2(−0.4)·3=−2.4. Each addition has local derivative 1, so each retained state receives −0.8 and each of the three uses contributes −0.8 to the same w. Two steps give s2=0.4, L2=(−0.6)^2=0.36. A final-only objective has no separate L1 or L2 term and no fourth application. To check the absence of a universal other-depth guarantee, even this simple family has w=1/3 with L3=0 while L2=L4=1/9; therefore perfect final-only fitting need not imply perfect other-depth fitting. This counterexample does not claim every model is worse at another depth, nor that shared training cannot indirectly improve intermediate states.
